title: Smooth source local acyclicity for constructible complexes
statement:
Let $S$ be Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ be of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $X\xrightarrow{h}Y$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; put $f=gh$. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring killed by an integer $m$ invertible on $S$, and let $L\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ be a bounded constructible complex [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Let $x$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] of $X$ with $y=h(x)$ and $s=f(x)$, let $t$ be a geometric point of $S$, and let $c:S_{(t)}\to S_{(s)}$ be a specialization, i.e. a morphism of $S$-schemes between the strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Using $c$ and the canonical maps $X_{(x)}\to Y_{(y)}\to S_{(s)}$, form the fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] $X_{x,c}=X_{(x)}\times_{S_{(s)}}S_{(t)}$ and $Y_{y,c}=Y_{(y)}\times_{S_{(s)}}S_{(t)}$, and let $h_{x,c}:X_{x,c}\to Y_{y,c}$ be the morphism induced by $h$. The canonical pullback map along $h_{x,c}$ is an isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(Y_{y,c},L|_{Y_{y,c}})\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(X_{x,c},(h^*L)|_{X_{x,c}}),$$
where derived sections and inverse images are taken in the derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. It is natural in $L$.

source.place: Proposition 0GJQ (label proposition-smooth-locally-acyclic) and its proof: Lemma 0EZU (lemma-base-change-f-star-general-stalks) applied to the base change of h over Y_(y) and the qcqs map Y_(y) x_{S_(s)} S_(t) -> Y_(y), together with smooth base change Theorem 0EYU (theorem-smooth-base-change) in its bounded-below derived form for torsion prime to the residue characteristics.

proof.text: Put $A=Y_{(y)}$, $C=S_{(s)}$, $D=S_{(t)}$, and $T=A\times_C D=Y_{y,c}$. All three strict localizations are affine by [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus $c:D\to C$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), and its base change $j:T\to A$ is qcqs by (3). If $S$ is empty there is no $x$, so the assertion is vacuous. Otherwise invertibility of $m$ forces $m\ne0$; put $N=|m|\ge1$. Then $N\Lambda=0$, and the inverse of $m$ pulls back to an inverse of $m$ on $A$, so $N$ is invertible on $A$.

source.place: Tags 0GJQ (proposition-smooth-locally-acyclic), qcqs hypothesis in 0EZU (lemma-base-change-f-star-general-stalks); Tags 00E8 and 01KO for affine qcqs

proof.text: Let $E=X\times_Y A$, with projections $p:E\to X$ and $r:E\to A$. It is a base change of $h$, hence smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). The canonical closed-point lift $a$ of $y$ to $A$, composed with the field map from the geometric point $x$, gives $\xi=(x,a)\in E$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-base-closed-point-localizations] to $h:X\to Y$, with $\bar s=y$, $S'=A$, $\bar x'=\xi$ and the identity map between the common geometric fields. It gives $A_{(a)}\simeq A$ and $E_{(\xi)}\simeq X_{(x)}$; its compatibility clause identifies the induced map to $A$ with $h_{(x)}:X_{(x)}\to Y_{(y)}$ followed by the inverse of its middle isomorphism $\varphi:A\to Y_{(y)}$. Here $\varphi$ is the identity of $A=Y_{(y)}$: both the functorial map $A_{(a)}\to Y_{(y)}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3) for the structure map $A\to Y$ and the canonical map $A_{(a)}\to A=Y_{(y)}$ are local, have the same composite to $Y$, and induce on residue fields the identity of $\kappa(\bar y)=\kappa(a)=\kappa(\bar a)$ inside the common geometric field; by the uniqueness in (3) they are equal. Hence the map $E_{(\xi)}\simeq X_{(x)}\to A$ is exactly $h_{(x)}$, and its composite to $C$ is the canonical map $X_{(x)}\to Y_{(y)}\to S_{(s)}$. Set $B=X_{(x)}$ and $V=B\times_A T$.

source.place: Tag 0GIP (lemma-base-change-strict-henselization-quasi-finite), case (2); the strict-base replacement in the first paragraph of the proof of etale-cohomology Tag 0GJQ

proof.text: The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $V=B\times_A(A\times_C D)$ with $B\times_C D=X_{x,c}$. Explicitly, a map into the first product is a pair of maps to $B$ and $D$ whose maps to $C$ agree: its map to $A$ is forced to be $h_{(x)}$ of the map to $B$. The inverse sends such a pair to the map into $A\times_C D$ given by $h_{(x)}$ and the map to $D$. Both composites fix the projections. Under this identification $u:V\to T$ is exactly $h_{x,c}$. The projections to $Y$ satisfy $\pi_Yu=h\pi_X$, so the inverse-image composition isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] identify $u^{-1}(L|_T)$ with $(h^*L)|_V$; for modules these are the same constant-coefficient inverse images by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](1)--(3).

First let $F$ be any abelian etale sheaf on $T$ annihilated by $N$. Every element of every stalk is killed by $N$, which is invertible on $A$. Apply [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] to the Cartesian square with smooth side $r:E\to A$ and qcqs side $j:T\to A$. For every $q\ge0$ the canonical sheaf exchange is an isomorphism. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-strict-local-cohomology] to this same square and take its test at $\xi$. It gives the canonical pullback isomorphism
$$H^q(A_{(a)}\times_A T,F)\longrightarrow H^q(E_{(\xi)}\times_A T,F).$$
By Step 2 these are $H^q(T,F)$ and $H^q(V,u^{-1}F)$, and the tested map is precisely $u^*$. Thus $u^*$ is an isomorphism in every nonnegative degree for every such $F$; no constructibility of $F$ is needed.

proof.text: Use abelian coefficients temporarily. On $D^+(T_{\mathrm{Et}})$ put $P(K)=R\Gamma(T,K)$ and $Q(K)=R\Gamma(V,u^{-1}K)$, with $\alpha_K:P(K)\to Q(K)$ the canonical pullback. These are triangulated functors: use [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] with the global-sections functors. The categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. The unit/Leray formula [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit](2) specifies $\alpha$. It commutes with shifts and gives morphisms of distinguished triangles: on complexes the unit is degreewise, hence its map on $\operatorname{Cone}(v)^i=K'^i\oplus K^{i+1}$ is the direct sum of its maps on the two summands; naturality with $v$ makes it commute with the off-diagonal entry $v$ in the cone differential. The resolution comparisons preserve this equality in the derived category. Additivity of sections and the cone formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] then give the three commuting triangle squares, including the shifted last square. This checks the triangle compatibility rather than inferring it from naturality alone.

source.place: Tags 01F8 (lemma-functoriality), 01F9 (equation-functorial-derived), 01FB (remark-explain-arrow); derived.tex Tag 05SE (proposition-derived-functor) and cone definition

proof.text:
For a sheaf $F$ killed by $N$ in degree zero, $H^q(\alpha_F)$ is the map of Step 4, by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit](2). It is an isomorphism for $q\ge0$; in negative degrees both complexes have zero cohomology, since they are computed by nonnegative injective resolutions. Hence $\alpha_F$ is an isomorphism, and so is $\alpha_{F[-b]}$ for every integer $b$ by Step 5. For a bounded abelian complex $K$ whose cohomology is killed by $N$, choose bounds $a\le b$ and induct on $b-a+1$. The zero complex is the base case. The standard truncation triangle [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]
$$\tau_{\le b-1}K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow\mathcal H^b(K)[-b]\longrightarrow(\tau_{\le b-1}K)[1]$$
has first term with cohomology in $[a,b-1]$ and third term a shifted sheaf killed by $N$; these assertions follow immediately by taking kernels and images in the defining good truncations. By induction the first comparison is invertible, and the shifted-sheaf case gives the third. Step 5 supplies a morphism between the two image triangles; [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes its middle arrow $\alpha_K$ invertible. This proves the comparison for every bounded abelian $K$ with $N$-annihilated cohomology.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle) and Tag 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle); sheaf case from etale-cohomology Tags 0EYU and 0EZU

proof.text: Let $K=L|_T$ in the module derived category. By bounded constructibility [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], $L$ has cohomology in a finite interval $[a,b]$. Exactness of constant-coefficient inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] gives the same bound for $K$. Forgetting coefficients is exact and commutes with cohomology by [lem-kun-unbounded-abelian-exchange-comparison], so its underlying abelian complex $K_{\mathrm{Ab}}$ is bounded; every cohomology stalk is killed by $N$ since $N\Lambda=0$. Step 6 makes its canonical pullback invertible. The terminal-object comparison [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget], applied on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{Et}}$, identifies the forgotten module-derived sections with the abelian ones and explicitly commutes with the canonical global-cohomology pullback. Its hypotheses hold: the coefficient sheaves are constant, both sites have terminal objects, and enough injectives is [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Consequently the underlying abelian map of $R\Gamma(T,K)\to R\Gamma(V,u^{-1}K)$ is the isomorphism of Step 6. It follows that the module map is an isomorphism: forgetting scalar structure detects kernels and cokernels degreewise, so it detects an acyclic cone and therefore a quasi-isomorphism in $D(\Lambda)$. Step 3 now identifies this exact map and both coefficients with the map displayed in the item.

source.place: Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), extended to bounded-below complexes by derived.tex Tag 05TA (proposition-enough-acyclics); constant-coefficient inverse images

proof.text: Finally $L\mapsto L|_T$ is a functor, and $\alpha$ is the unit-defined natural transformation of Step 5. For a morphism $L\to L'$, naturality of the unit says that pullback after the induced map on $R\Gamma(T,-)$ equals the induced map on $R\Gamma(V,-)$ after pullback. The coefficient-forgetting comparisons in Step 7 are natural and commute with these pullbacks, while the inverse-image composition comparisons in Step 3 are natural in their coefficient. Hence these same equalities hold for the displayed $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism, proving its naturality in $L$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N1-869fcf15e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 27 cited statements, the parent (its step 2 is the only user) and Stacks 0GJQ/0EZU (etale-cohomology.tex l.19167 ff., l.16497 ff.). No SGA is cited. There are no new nodes. The statement is unchanged and true: smooth base change for X x_Y Y_(y) -> Y_(y) along the qcqs map T = Y_(y) x_{S_(s)} S_(t) -> Y_(y), followed by the 0EZU strict-local test at the lifted point, gives the sheaf case for any N-torsion F. That is the 0GJQ argument with an arbitrary sheaf in place of Z/n, honestly marked as agent-written. Truncation induction (triangle, base and step all stated), the scalar-forgetting comparison and conservativity carry it to bounded module complexes; constructibility is used only for boundedness. The coefficient category is the Lambda-module derived category, not silently identified with the abelian one. Small cases pass: empty S, h = id, t = s with c = id, L = 0, a shifted single sheaf. No duplicate found (0GJQ/local-acyclicity grep over the DAG; the smooth-local-acyclicity, locally-constant-torsion, geometric-fibre-test and nearby-smooth-source-exchange nodes all differ). I accept the 12 declared generic tool uses. One fault, fixed (E5/C3): Step 2 claimed the map E_(xi) ~ X_(x) -> A is h_(x) without showing that the middle isomorphism phi: A -> Y_(y) of lem-weil-pbc-strict-base-closed-point-localizations is the identity. Without it, neither V ~ X_{x,c} over S_(s) nor u = h_{x,c} follows. The fix adds the argument from the uniqueness clause (3) of lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality: the functorial map A_(a) -> Y_(y) and the canonical map j_A are both local, agree over Y and induce the identity on residue fields, so they are equal. It adds that citation to step 2 uses, proof_deps and split_report.tool_uses; the corrected node is under fixes/. Details are in review.md.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
